Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and brilliant detective known for his keen observation skills and dedication to uncovering the truth.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend, assistant, and the narrator of the stories who aspires to document Byomkesh's cases.

Kumar Tridib Narayan Roy.description: A wealthy young man from North Bengal who seeks Byomkesh's help in recovering his family's stolen diamond.

Sir Digindra Narayan Roy.description: A wealthy, eccentric genius known for his artistic and scientific pursuits who is suspected of stealing a family diamond.

Ujre Singh.description: A loyal Nepali servant and chawkidar (watchman) at Sir Digindra's house, known for his vigilance.

Putiram.description: Ajit and Byomkesh's servant, who assists with household matters and delivers messages.

Seemanta Heera.description: The name of the chapter, referring to the legendary family diamond at the center of the mystery.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, referenced as the setting for the story.

Calcutta.description: The capital city of West Bengal, now known as Kolkata; a major urban center in the story.

North Bengal.description: A geographic region in the northern part of West Bengal, India, where Kumar's estate is located.

Baroda.description: A princely state in western India, referenced as one of the royal families displaying jewels at the exhibition.

Hyderabad.description: A former princely state in southern India, also referenced for its royal jewels.

Patiala.description: A princely state in Punjab, India, mentioned in the context of the exhibition of royal jewels.

Moghuls.description: The Mughal dynasty, historical rulers of much of India, during whose reign Kumar's ancestors received their land.

Paris.description: The capital of France, where Sir Digindra's statue was exhibited and acclaimed.

Louvre.description: The famous art museum in Paris, where the original Nataraj statue is kept.

Grand Hotel.description: A well-known hotel in Calcutta where Kumar stays during his visit.

National Library.description: A major library in Calcutta, visited by Byomkesh for research.

Calcutta University.description: A prestigious university in Calcutta, referenced during the job interview scene.

Nataraj.description: A depiction of Lord Shiva as the cosmic dancer, central to the mystery as a statue; the Nataraj statue represents Lord Shiva in his cosmic dance form.

babu.description: A respectful term of address for men, often used in Bengal.

Bahadur.description: An honorific title, often used to denote respect or nobility.

Dewan.description: A steward or manager, especially of finances, in a wealthy household.

chawkidar.description: A watchman or guard, commonly employed for security.

almirah.description: A wardrobe or cupboard, used for storing valuables or clothes.

phiran.description: A traditional loose cloak worn in Kashmir, referenced as Sir Digindra's attire.
